approvedBasis: User rejected the fairy-tale feeling of v01 and requested relatively realistic visuals similar to the Steam game PC Building Simulator. Portrait, isometric workshop and close-up case workbench remain in scope.
candidateOnly: Art direction review board, not approved runtime assets, layered source art or validated component geometry. No economy or supplier values are changed.
prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Edit target: the supplied Orangegame v01 review board. Retain only the three-panel subject structure: a portrait-framed small computer assembly workshop on the left, a large open upright computer case close-up in the middle, and a standalone graphics board procurement-card image on the right. Completely re-render the visual style into relatively realistic industrial PC assembly simulator game art, using PC Building Simulator-like believable material response, natural proportions and clean practical lighting. This is a substantial style revision, not a gentle recolor. Remove illustrated ink outlines, cartoon shading, cream scrapbook framing, honey-orange room grading, toy proportions and decorative foliage. Make the left workshop a practical modest 2016 commercial PC assembly room: neutral light-grey walls, realistic steel-framed laminate workbench, dark antistatic mat, monitor, tool pegboard, metal storage shelves, plain brown component boxes, screwdriver, practical cable spools. Show an orthographic isometric room view with realistic object sizes and clear usable working space; no cinematic wide-angle distortion. In the center, use a realistic black or graphite mid-tower, thin painted steel case panels, real screw heads, folded sheet metal, ventilation holes, matte PCB and plastic, finely ridged metal heat sink and believable soft reflections. Correct the assembly geometry: motherboard mounted to its tray, RAM next to CPU cooler, a conventional graphics card in a horizontal PCIe slot with its rear bracket aligned to case expansion openings; the graphics card fans face DOWN, so the side close-up shows its thin long side edge and the cooler below, not two fan faces wrongly rotated toward the camera. Front intake fans face the front panel and are perpendicular to the motherboard tray; show them at their plausible installed angle. Power supply sits at the bottom, storage mounts and cables look physical and connected. Dark cables dominate with restrained orange accents; no rainbow LEDs. Leave tiny blank manufacturer sticker areas. The right panel uses a charcoal-grey squared product-card field, a realistic unbranded 2016-era dual-fan graphics board at a product-photo three-quarter angle, generous blank space for later engine-rendered labels, no decorative paper card. Shared style: natural physical shading like a restrained real-time 3D game render, moderate roughness, readable material differences, realistic edges, subtle practical wear, no excessive dirt or ruined warehouse mood. Shared palette: cool-neutral grey, graphite, black rubber, muted metal, brown cardboard and only small orange brand accents. Lighting: neutral overhead workshop light plus modest daylight fill; interfaces and cable routes remain visible, no bloom, sun rays, deep vignette or dramatic shallow depth of field. Keep all panels sharply readable at phone scale and unify their material and lighting vocabulary. No captions, text, labels, numerals, real manufacturer logos or watermark. This remains an original Orangegame art direction concept board, not a copied game screenshot or a functional UI.
